title: AvalancheBench: Evaluating Enterprise Agent-Driven Semantic Query Processing Through Latent World Recovery
abstract: arXiv:2605.24183v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As LLMs improve, data agents are emerging as a new interface for analytics, while semantic query processing engines use LLMs to operate over structured and unstructured data. Existing benchmarks largely evaluate agents and semantic query engines in isolation, leaving it unclear whether agents can decide when and how to use semantic operators in end-to-end analysis.   We introduce AvalancheBench, a multimodal enterprise analytics benchmark that generates observed data from latent world specifications and evaluates data agents on their ability to recover that world. The benchmark's 3 validated tasks contain 58 questions spanning text, images, and documents. Questions are provided together as a multi-part analytical brief and may share intermediate results, exposing the avalanche effect: errors can propagate through legitimate dependencies, and inappropriate reuse can cause otherwise unrelated questions to fail. translated_title: AvalancheBench：通过潜在世界恢复评估企业级智能体驱动的语义查询处理
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型（LLM）能力的提升，数据智能体正成为数据分析的新接口，而语义查询处理引擎则利用LLM对结构化和非结构化数据进行操作。现有基准测试大多将智能体与语义查询引擎分开评估，因此智能体能否在端到端分析中决定何时以及如何使用语义算子仍不清楚。我们提出了AvalancheBench，这是一个多模态企业分析基准，它从潜在世界规范生成观测数据，并据此评估数据智能体恢复该潜在世界的能力。该基准包含3个经过验证的任务，共58个问题，涵盖文本、图像和文档。这些问题以多部分分析简报的形式一并提供，且可能共享中间结果，从而暴露出“雪崩效应”：错误可以通过合法的依赖关系传播，而不恰当的复用会导致原本互不相关的问题失败。AvalancheBench测……（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了AvalancheBench，一个从潜在世界规范生成观测数据、通过涵盖文本、图像和文档的58个多部分问题评估数据智能体端到端语义查询能力的多模态企业分析基准，并首次揭示了错误经合法依赖关系传播、不当复用中间结果导致无关问题失败的“雪崩效应”。
en_tdlr: AvalancheBench is a multimodal enterprise analytics benchmark that generates observed data from latent world specifications to evaluate whether data agents can recover that world in end-to-end semantic query processing, exposing an "avalanche effect" in which errors propagate through legitimate dependencies and inappropriate reuse of shared intermediate results causes otherwise unrelated questions to fail.
